title: Israel Extension
description: Israeli succession rules: parallel court systems (civil family court, rabbinical, sharia, druze), Inheritance Law 1965 process types, religious authority orders, kibbutz/moshav communal property, and Holocaust restitution assets.
dataProvenance: Inheritance Law 1965 (Chok HaYerusha), Succession Ordinance, Family Court Law 1995, Rabbinical Courts Jurisdiction (Marriage and Divorce) Law 1953

parallelCourtSystems.description: The adjudicating court system handling this succession matter. Israel operates parallel civil and religious court systems, each with jurisdiction over different communities and matter types.

adjudicatingCourt.description: The court system with jurisdiction over this succession matter. civil_family_court: Family Court under Family Court Law 1995 (default for most succession matters). rabbinical_court: Rabbinical Court with jurisdiction over Jewish personal status and succession where all parties consent. sharia_court: Sharia Court with jurisdiction over Muslim personal status matters. druze_court: Druze Religious Court with jurisdiction over Druze personal status. registrar_of_inheritance: Registrar of Inheritance (Rasham HaYerushot) for uncontested applications.

courtOrderReference.description: Reference number of the court order or application

allPartiesConsented.description: Whether all parties have consented to this court's jurisdiction (relevant where jurisdiction is consent-based, e.g. rabbinical court for Jewish parties)

inheritanceLaw1965.description: Details of the succession process under the Inheritance Law 1965 (Chok HaYerusha). The law provides two tracks: tzevu kiyum (probate order for wills) and tzevu yerusha (succession order for intestate estates).

successionOrderType.description: Type of succession order sought or obtained. tzevu_kiyum: probate order (tzav kiyum tzava'a) confirming the validity of a will. tzevu_yerusha: succession order (tzav yerusha) determining heirs on intestacy. combined: both orders sought together, e.g. where a partial will exists.

objectionPeriodExpired.description: Whether the statutory objection period (14 days from publication of the application notice) has expired without objection

objectionsReceived.description: Whether any objections were received during the objection period

spouseEntitlement.description: Surviving spouse entitlement under Inheritance Law 1965. On intestacy, the spouse's share depends on the class of heirs surviving alongside them.

moveableFraction.description: Spouse's share of moveable property as a fraction, e.g. 1/2

immoveableFraction.description: Spouse's share of immoveable property as a fraction, e.g. 1/2

dwellingRightGranted.description: Whether the spouse has been granted a dwelling right (zchut dirah) in the matrimonial home under section 11(a) of the Inheritance Law

religiousAuthorityOrder.description: An order or ruling issued by a religious court with jurisdiction over this succession matter. Applicable where a religious court has issued a binding ruling recognised under Israeli law.

authority.description: The religious authority issuing the order. bet_din: Rabbinical court (Jewish law). sharia_court: Sharia court (Islamic law). druze_court: Druze religious court.

orderType.description: Type of religious authority order. succession_ruling: ruling on intestate distribution. halachic_will_validation: validation of a will under halachic principles. waqf_ruling: ruling concerning waqf (Islamic religious endowment) assets. consent_order: order by consent of all parties.

orderReference.description: Reference number of the religious authority order

orderDate.description: Date of the religious authority order

binding.description: Whether the religious authority order is binding on all parties and recognised by civil courts

kibbutzProperty.description: Communal or cooperative property held through a kibbutz or moshav. These structures create special succession rules as membership rights, housing allocations, and production quotas may not be freely transferable.

communalOwnershipType.description: Type of communal or cooperative structure. kibbutz_communal: traditional collective kibbutz where all property is collectively owned. kibbutz_renewed: renewed (mתחדש) kibbutz operating on differential pay and partial private ownership. moshav: cooperative smallholder settlement where land is state-leased and individually farmed. moshav_shitufi: collective moshav combining kibbutz production with moshav family life.

membershipRightsTransferable.description: Whether membership rights in the communal organisation are transferable to heirs

communityName.description: Name of the kibbutz or moshav

personalPropertyValue.description: Estimated value of the deceased's personal property held outside communal ownership, in minor currency units

holocaustRestitution.description: Holocaust restitution assets — property or claims arising from Nazi persecution and subsequent restitution programmes. Israel has a significant number of estates involving Holocaust-era assets due to its founding population.

restitutionAssetsExist.description: Whether the estate includes known or suspected Holocaust restitution assets or claims

restitutionSource.description: Source programme or authority from which restitution is or was sought. claims_conference: Conference on Jewish Material Claims Against Germany. german_government: German federal or state government restitution. austrian_government: Austrian government restitution. swiss_banks_settlement: Swiss Banks Settlement (Volcker process). art_restitution: looted art restitution. property_restitution: real property restitution. other: other restitution programme.

originalOwnerKnown.description: Whether the identity of the original pre-war owner is known and documented

ongoingClaims.description: Whether there are ongoing restitution claims or applications that have not yet been resolved

estimatedValue.description: Estimated value of known restitution assets or settled claims in minor currency units
